leanback.tagline: Your PC, now a couch console.
leanback.problem: Using a PC on the TV is clumsy: tiny text, a pointer you can't find, and a keyboard you don't want on your lap. Leanback Mode notices when you pick up a controller and rearranges Windows for the couch.
bullets: Switches to Leanback mode the moment your controller turns on, and back to desktop mode when you switch it off
Controller dozed off mid-movie? You stay in Leanback mode until you turn it off yourself
Bigger text and a pointer you can actually see from across the room
Sticks move and scroll, buttons click, go back and open Start
Steps aside on its own when you launch a game
Works with Xbox, PlayStation, Switch Pro, 8BitDo and generic Bluetooth or 2.4 GHz pads
leanback.alt: A TV showing large, couch-friendly Windows tiles and a big pointer, with a game controller in front of it

mediatabjump.tagline: Who's making that noise? Found it.
mediatabjump.problem: Thirty tabs open and something is playing. Windows shows you what is playing, but not where. Media Tab Jump makes the player in the volume flyout a shortcut straight to the right tab.
bullets: Click the now-playing card and land on the exact tab, even in another window
Works with Edge, Chrome, Brave, Firefox, Opera and Vivaldi
A soft, color-shifting glow tells you the card is clickable
Play, pause and skip buttons keep working like always
No browser extension, nothing to sign in to
mediatabjump.alt: The Windows volume flyout with a glowing now-playing card, and an arrow to the browser tab that is playing

autozoom.tagline: Every app at a comfortable size.
autozoom.problem: An app that looks great full-screen can feel cramped in half the screen, and the other way round. AutoZoom lets you pick how zoomed in each app is when its window is maximized and when it isn't, and switches by itself as you resize.
bullets: Any app that zooms with Ctrl and +: Claude, Teams, Discord, Slack, VS Code, Notepad, browsers
Two levels per app: one for maximized, one for everything else
Each window keeps its own zoom, so two windows of the same app never fight
Add apps and set their zoom from the tray app, with changes applied instantly
Never reads the screen or what you type: it only presses the app's own zoom keys
autozoom.alt: The same app shown twice: maximized with larger text, and in a smaller window with text sized to fit

toolkit.tagline: Every tool, one tidy tray icon.
toolkit.problem: Small helpers are great until you have five tray icons and five settings files. The toolkit tray app puts every tool behind one icon, with quick switches and a settings page for each.
bullets: Click once to flip between Leanback mode and desktop mode, or turn any tool on or off
Tune controller speed, scrolling and what every button does, without touching a config file
Pick the hover glow's colour, brightness and size, with a live preview
Choose which apps AutoZoom handles and how big each one gets
Light or dark, your Windows accent or one of nine colours, three tray icon styles
Pause everything for an hour when you need a plain PC
toolkit.alt: The toolkit's tray menu: a Leanback mode card, tiles for Leanback Mode, Controller mouse, Media Tab Jump and Hover glow, and a Pause everything button
